author: edu-critic-kestrel (independent education critic, Claude Opus 5.5 subagent)

findings.claim: E1/E3/E5: the Activity 3 editor turns syntax errors into misleading verdicts. Exercised headless at 570 px from a correct solution: (1) Deleting the ';' after 'this.event = event' (line 6) gives 'No problems found', with the Output row 'event is not set from its parameter yet', the warning-toned verdict 'Almost: 4 of 5 checks pass', and the message 'You have one more checked try'. The learner is told a correct assignment does not set the field, and loses one of the two checked tries (the same happens for line 7 and seat). (2) Deleting the ';' after 'this(event, 0)' gives 'All 5 checks pass' and Done for code javac rejects. (3) 'int seat = 0' without ';' on line 3 is reported as 'Error, line 12 … Add a semicolon (;) at the end of line 12', pointing at the class's closing lines. A career-changer reading 'event is not set' while looking at 'this.event = event' cannot work out the real problem. This is the near-miss nudge pointing at the wrong detail, the opposite of what policy 1.1 and 1.3 intend.
findings.recommendation: Run the semicolon/statement-shape parse before the checks and report a missing ';' as a Problem at the line that lacks it, without using a try (as the page already does for missing braces). Never emit 'Almost' or a check failure when the real cause is a parse problem. Add committed starter/malformed routes for these three cases.

findings.claim: C1/C2/G3: Activity 2 asks the learner to judge six compile-or-not scenarios, and its reading column has no code block. The only worked code, the buggy Point class, is in Activity 1, and that section is hidden once Activity 2 opens. Yet the teaching refers to 'this.x = x;' and 'new Point()' as if Point were on screen. The corrected Point constructor (this.x = x; this.y = y;) is never shown. The default-constructor rule, which is the subject of the sort, is given only in prose. A beginner sorting 'Mug(int ml) declared, then new Mug()' has no worked example of a declared constructor next to the calls that do and do not match it.
findings.recommendation: Add one short code block to Activity 2's teaching: the corrected Point constructor, then two lines in main, 'new Point(3, 4)' (compiles) and 'new Point()' (does not compile once a constructor is declared), each with a comment. Keep it Point-based so the Cup/Mug/Jar/Pot answers are not given.

location.selector: ## Model; ## Cheat sheet; ## Static interaction alternatives > ### explore

findings.claim: Markdown companion (generated by authoring/tools/qa/md-from-html.mjs; regenerating it from the current HTML gives identical bytes). (1) It has no On the job card: the decision, the boundary, At work and In interviews are missing (A1, A2), and so are the task lead lines. (2) The first teaching paragraph of Activity 2 is moved out of order under a '## Model' heading after Activity 4's text. 'Model' is authoring vocabulary, not a learner heading (B4). (3) The hints and the Challenge are listed under '## Cheat sheet' with orphaned labels ('Another hint Another hint, 2 of 2 for Activity 3'). (4) The Ticket.java starter in '### explore' is flattened onto one line, so the '//' comments swallow the code after them.
findings.recommendation: Fix in a tooling branch (md-from-html.mjs): keep teaching in source order with no 'Model' heading, emit the On the job rows and task leads, put hints and the challenge under their activity, keep fenced starter code, and use learner headings instead of engine types. Then regenerate this companion.

findings.claim: A2/G4 authenticity: the boundary is 'Many optional values would need many constructors; write named static methods that return a new object.' The clause does explain the alternative, and static methods were taught earlier. But practitioners usually answer 'many optional values' with a builder. Named static methods mainly help when a few combinations need clear names, so they also multiply as optional values grow. A beginner may carry away a weak rule. The SME critic should confirm the technical framing.
findings.recommendation: Either narrow the condition to what static methods solve ('Two shortcuts take the same parameter types, so overloads cannot tell them apart; write named static methods that return a new object instead'), or keep 'many optional values' and name a builder in a clause, as a pattern met later in the course.

findings.claim: A4/A1: the In interviews row, 'Expect "when does Java supply a default constructor?"', is exactly what Activities 2 and 4 practise. The page does not say so: Activity 4 is framed as 'A reviewer asks', and the row does not point to either activity, as DESIGN.md's On the job rule asks ('Point to the activity when it practises exactly that probe'). The row also sits on Activity 3's card about chaining, so it reads as disconnected from the decision above it.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Activity 4 practises this.' to the In interviews row, or frame Activity 4's lead as an interviewer's question, as classes-and-objects does with its counting question.

findings.claim: B1: two terms are used without definition. The Activity 3 check label 'The one-parameter constructor delegates with `this(...)` as its first statement' uses 'delegates', which the page never defines; the teaching says 'call another constructor'. The Activity 2 scenario 'a form handler calls new Pot("big")' uses 'form handler', which this Java course has not taught. It is decoration, but a beginner may stop on it.
findings.recommendation: Write 'calls the two-parameter constructor with this(...) as its first statement', and replace 'a form handler' with plain words such as 'new code'.

findings.claim: E1/B5: with lanes named 'Compiles' and 'Does not compile', a wrong press opens with 'Not Does not compile.' (observed when Cup was placed in Does not compile). The verdict is a garbled double negative, which a beginner has to decode before reading the reason.
findings.recommendation: Word the wrong-lane verdict as 'Not this lane: …', or quote the lane name ('Not "Does not compile": …'). The text is page-owned in the engine script.

findings.claim: G7: in the 570 px frame the Ticket.java starter comments overflow the editor (textarea scrollWidth 543 px against clientWidth 435 px), so the numbered instruction comments are cut off unless the learner scrolls sideways inside the editor.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the starter comments at about 48 characters.

findings.claim: B5/G1: the completion recap names activities 'Default constructors', 'Write constructors' and 'Final check'. The lesson path calls them 'Spot the lines that break the build', 'Write the constructors for a Ticket' and 'Pick the line that compiles', so a learner told to 'open one and use Restart activity' cannot match them.
findings.recommendation: Use the lesson-path titles as the PEP_PAGE labels, or have the recap show the path row text.
